facts.value: 380 towing companies hold non-consent tow permits listed on the city roster with business emails; every permit expires on 31 December and must be renewed with an inspection packet. 150 have been contacted; 230 have not.
Sell A complete renewal packet: vehicle inspection schedule, insurance certificate checklist and filled renewal forms to each buyer.
Pilot invoices (Oct 2026): 24 towing companies paid $420 for a permit renewal packet.

reviews.reasons: The commercial chain holds: $420 is a real purchase price paid by 24 towing companies (Oct 2026 pilot invoices); conversion 24/150 = 16% on this offer's own sales; 230 uncontacted roster companies x 16% = ~37 vs 15 needed (15 x $420 = $6,300; plan uses 16 = $6,720); permits expire 31 Dec, inside the window; cost $5 < $420; settlement 4 days. The exclusion of the owner-delivered claim reviews is correct (4 x 6 h = 24 h > 10 h allowance). But this goal's binding limit is 2 owner hours per week, and the plan records ownerHours = 0 as EVIDENCED citing the delivery fact, while the same card records humanHours 0.5 per deal (the same field that records 6 h per deal on the owner-delivered opening). 16 deals x 0.5 h = 8 h. As scheduled (all packets delivered on day 8, collected day 10) that is ~8 h in one week against a 2 h/week limit. Treating a recorded 0.5 h/deal as zero is an unknown/contradicted figure treated as known, on the one limit this goal sets.
findings: ownerHours quantity is wrong: card humanHours 0.5 per deal gives 8 h for 16 deals (7.5 h for the 15 actually needed), not 0. The plan must carry it and schedule it inside 2 h/week: at most 4 deals delivered per week, e.g. 4/week over weeks 1-4 (8 h total, never more than 2 h in a week), last batch delivered by ~day 28 and settled by ~day 32 < 35; or show evidence that the 0.5 h is not owner time.

Ledger/step timing: the deliver step carries $80 on day 8 while the ledger books it on day 15 'after receipts settle'; the contract has no exposure cap here, so this is cosmetic, but step and ledger should agree.
Once hours are scheduled, the receipt rows must be split by batch with their own settle days rather than one $6,720 receipt on day 10.
SEND_A_MESSAGE and ISSUE_AN_INVOICE are NOT_CONNECTED; routine connections needed before day 1.

reviews.reasons: The ledger/step and batch fixes are accepted, and the commercial chain still holds ($420 paid by 24 companies; 24/150 = 16%; 230 uncontacted x 16% = ~37 vs 15 needed; $5 cost; 4-day settlement; permits expire 31 Dec). The rebuttal on owner hours does not settle it. The card field is humanHours = 0.5 per deal: hours a human spends, which by definition is not Brain's production time. No human other than the owner is recorded on this opening, and Brain's own check of this revision maps the Deliver step to owner PERSON (currentCheck.brain.steps: 'Deliver ... owner: PERSON, cost 5'), which is a specific record contradicting the reading that the 0.5 h belongs to Brain. On a goal whose only limit is 2 owner hours per week, a recorded 0.5 human hour per deal cannot be booked as EVIDENCED 0. It is at best unknown, and as recorded it is 8 h for 16 deals; the plan's schedule (16 packets produced on day 9) would put ~8 h in one week. The fix is cheap and keeps the target: pace delivery at <= 4 packets per week (<= 2 h/week), 4/week over weeks 1-4 = 16 packets, last batch delivered ~day 28 and settled ~day 32 < 35; 15 packets already reach $6,300.
findings: ownerHours: carry 0.5 h per deal as the owner's (or as UNKNOWN with a pace that fits even if it is the owner's), not EVIDENCED 0; schedule at most 4 deliveries per week.

Payment terms: the plan now invoices 'on order and collect before production', but the pilot evidence (24 paid invoices, 4 days to first cash) does not state prepayment. The goal has no exposure cap, so pay-on-delivery also works, but prepayment is a new assumption and should either be evidenced or replaced by pay-on-delivery with settle = delivery + 4 days.
Step/ledger: the single deliver step on day 9 spends for all 16 packets while the second batch of 8 is only ordered on day 12; split delivery by batch to match the receipts.

reviews.reasons: The earlier findings are resolved. Owner hours: the card's 0.5 human hours per packet is now carried, and delivery is paced at 4 packets per week in weeks 1-4 (days 7, 14, 21, 28), so even counted entirely as owner time it is exactly 2 h/week and 8 h total, inside the 2 h/week (10 h over 35 days) limit. The plan holds under either reading of who spends those hours. Payment is on delivery per the pilot, settling 4 days later (days 11, 18, 25, 32 <= 35). Recomputed: 4 x 4 x $420 = $6,720 >= $6,000; 15 packets ($6,300) suffice, so batch 4 needs only 3 of its 4. Direct cost 16 x $5 = $80; the $20 owner advance for batch 1 is allowed (no capital cap in this contract) and is recovered on day 11. Demand: 230 uncontacted roster companies x 16% = ~37 vs 16 needed; every permit expires 31 Dec (day 34), so demand is current through the window. The steps and ledger now match batch by batch. Exclusion of the owner-delivered claim reviews (24 h > 10 h) remains correct.
findings: Tight tail: the last batch settles on day 32 against a 35-day window, and the target needs it ($5,040 after three batches). Any 4-day slip in batch 4 misses the window. Deliver each batch as soon as its week's 4 orders arrive (e.g. days 5, 12, 19, 26) to widen the slack; the weekly hour pace is unchanged.
Week-4 buyers receive their packet on ~day 28 for a 31 December (day 34) expiry; confirm the city accepts renewals filed that late, or deliver the 4 latest-deadline companies in the earlier weeks.
